question: What is the primary goal of environmental hygiene in a community?

options.A: Ensuring every household has running hot water
options.B: Eliminating all microorganisms from outdoor public spaces
options.C: Preventing diseases by controlling environmental hazards
options.D: Reducing the cost of municipal waste collection

explanation: Environmental hygiene focuses on managing physical and biological factors in the surroundings to protect human health and prevent illness. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which practice best describes community sanitation?

options.A: Spraying insecticides to kill adult mosquitoes
options.B: Safe management and disposal of human excreta
options.C: Sweeping hospital floors three times a day
options.D: Testing borehole water for heavy metal toxins

explanation: Sanitation specifically refers to the hygienic management and disposal of human waste and wastewater to break disease transmission cycles. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which pathogen is commonly transmitted through contaminated drinking water?
explanation: Vibrio cholerae is the bacterium responsible for cholera, a severe diarrheal illness spread primarily through contaminated water sources. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why is boiling considered an effective water purification method?

options.A: Boiling completely removes all dissolved chemical minerals
options.B: It adds safe minerals back into untreated borehole water
options.C: High temperatures destroy pathogenic bacteria and viruses
options.D: Heat permanently dissolves heavy metals out of the water

explanation: Thermal energy disrupts cellular structures and proteins of harmful microorganisms, rendering them non-viable. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the safest way to dispose of used injection needles?

options.A: Burning them openly behind the healthcare clinic
options.B: Recapping them tightly and tossing them in sinks
options.C: Placing them into puncture-resistant safety boxes
options.D: Throwing them directly into general black plastic bags

explanation: Sharps containers prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to healthcare workers and waste handlers alike. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of waste segregation at the point of generation?

options.A: Ensuring all hospital refuse can be recycled into plastic products
options.B: Preventing hazardous clinical waste from mixing with domestic trash
options.C: Making municipal waste collection faster and cheaper for cities
options.D: Reducing the overall weight of garbage bins in patient wards

explanation: Sorting waste immediately prevents infectious or sharp materials from contaminating general refuse and endangering handlers. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which animal is the primary reservoir for transmitting Lassa fever?
explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys natalensis) sheds the Lassa virus in its urine and droppings, exposing humans through contaminated food or surfaces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h4)

question: How does clearing stagnant water around homes help control malaria?

options.A: It stops mosquitoes from flying long distances into towns
options.B: It destroys the breeding sites of mosquito larvae
options.C: It dries out the skin of adult female mosquitoes
options.D: It prevents adult mosquitoes from biting during the day

explanation: Female mosquitoes require standing water to lay eggs; removing these puddles breaks the reproductive cycle of the vector. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h4)

question: Which demographic group is most vulnerable to poor environmental hygiene and contaminated water?
explanation: Young children have developing immune systems and higher fluid turnover rates, making them exceptionally vulnerable to waterborne illnesses and dehydration. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h5)

question: How do poor sanitation conditions indirectly contribute to child malnutrition?

options.A: Dirty surroundings cause children to lose their natural appetite
options.B: Unclean air prevents the body from digesting proteins properly
options.C: Repeated intestinal infections reduce nutrient absorption in the gut
options.D: Flies and pests consume all the food stored in household kitchens

explanation: Chronic diarrhea and gut infections impair the body's ability to absorb essential vitamins and nutrients, leading to stunting and wasting. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of a nurse in environmental health?

options.A: Constructing municipal sewage treatment plants in cities
options.C: Educating families on safe water storage and handwashing
options.D: Manufacturing chemical insecticides for vector control

explanation: Nurses play a direct educational role, teaching patients and communities practical hygiene behaviors to prevent disease transmission. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h6)

question: A community nurse notices rising diarrhea cases in a local settlement. What should be the first action?

options.A: Wait for the municipal government to investigate the problem
options.B: Prescribe antibiotics to every household in the village
options.C: Assess local water sources and community sanitation practices
options.D: Order immediate demolition of all residential buildings

explanation: Identifying the root environmental cause through assessment guides targeted interventions like water testing and hygiene education. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h6)
